Elena — thanks for the redline. Routing to our legal for the definitive wording but wanted to give a short read from commercial:

Summary reading 
- We intended "floor" to mean a minimum monthly commitment expressed in $USD (not raw tokens). The table should therefore reference the minimum monthly $ value and include token bands only for billing rate tiers.
- The "stabilizer/recalculate" language was intended as an operational adjustment (to move customers between fee bands when actual usage deviates) with a 30-day notice and an annual true-up. If procurement needs quarterly true-ups or a rollback, we can discuss.

Proposed near-term approach
- I'll attach a short annotation doc with two suggested edits (ben_redline_annotations.docx).
- If legal is OK we can push a limited-scope amendment to address: explicit definition of "minimum monthly commitment", clarify whether banding is by $ or tokens, and add a one-time true-up mechanic with optional rollback cap.

Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow to sort level of granularity? I can include Marcus (finance) if you want to run dollars vs tokens modeling.

Ben / Rishi —

I reviewed Kestrel's redline and Ben's annotations. Below are proposed edits for Exhibit D that are tight and limited-scope (so we can do an amendment rather than re-negotiating the whole order form). I've included replacement text you can push to Kestrel.

1) Define the floor in USD
Replace any instance of "floor" with the defined term "Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC)" and add definition: "'Minimum Monthly Commitment' means the minimum aggregate $USD amount payable by Customer for Hosted Inference services in a calendar month as set forth in the Pricing Table."

2) Banding vs tokens
Clarify that billing tiers in Exhibit D reflect per-token rates associated with monthly $USD spend bands. Add sentence: "Per-token rates shall apply based on the aggregate MMC for the month; token usage in excess of the MMC shall be billed at the overage rates set forth in the Pricing Table."

3) True-up / rollback mechanics
Proposed language for a new subsection 2.3:

"2.3 True-up and Adjustment. On an annual basis (the "True-Up Date"), the parties shall reconcile actual usage against billed MMCs. For the first twelve (12) months following Effective Date, the parties may elect instead to perform quarterly reconciliations. Any overbilling shall be credited to Customer; any underbilling shall be invoiced. Notwithstanding the foregoing, adjustments to MMC shall not reduce previously invoiced amounts for periods prior to the True-Up Date except where gross billing errors are demonstrated."

Rationale: this preserves our commercial position (no retroactive crediting outside true-up) while offering quarterly reconciliation as an option during ramp. If Kestrel insists on full rollback, we can offer a limited rollback cap (e.g., 25% of the prior quarter's MMC) but I'd prefer to avoid that if finance objects.

4) Operational notice for band changes
Add a 30-day notice requirement before applying a band increase. For band decreases triggered by material sustained drops (>60 days) allow automatic move after 30 days with notice.

I attached a clean legal redline (Exhibit_D_clean_redline_legal_v2.docx) for your reference. Marcus, please confirm whether the rollback cap is acceptable vs a credit-only model.

Lauren Bishop
Associate General Counsel
Redwood Inference

Elena — looping back with our legal suggested edits (attached summary). Short highlights for procurement: 

- We propose to replace ambiguous "floor" language with "Minimum Monthly Commitment (MMC) in $USD" to avoid token vs dollar mismatch.
- We can offer quarterly true-ups during the first 12 months to support your ramp, then annual true-ups thereafter.
- To avoid surprise mid-term band shifts, we propose a 30-day operational notice for any band change; any true-up adjustments reconcile only prospectively except as set out in the limited rollback cap language.

Ben / Lauren —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the concise options. Procurement and our legal reviewed the redlines overnight. Quick replies inline:

- MMC in $USD: Agreed, that removes ambiguity.
- Quarterly true-ups for the first 12 months: Procurement prefers quarterly reconciliations for the first 18 months given our expected ramp variability. Would Redwood accept 18 months?
- Rollback cap: Procurement cannot accept any asymmetrical rollback that only favors Redwood. If a rollback cap is required, Kestrel proposes a mutual rollback mechanism capped at 30% of the prior quarter's MMC (both directions) and limited to the first 12 months post-Effective Date.

We attached a counterproposal with suggested language for 2.3 and the rollback matrix (Kestrel_counter_proposal.docx). Procurement also asks that the limited amendment include a clear example table demonstrating how banding and credits work for overage vs underage.

We are willing to sign the limited amendment via the DocuSign link if we get agreement on: (a) extend quarterly true-ups to 18 months, and (b) mutual rollback cap at 30% limited to first 12 months.

Forwarding procurement contact for any follow-ups: procurement@kestrelhealth.com

Attachments: Kestrel_counter_proposal.docx (docx)

— Elena
